title: Slipstream Neon
premise: A glowing futuristic interceptor races through a neon midnight corridor, weaving between hostile traffic for as long as possible.
interaction_model: Single-screen, real-time pointer/touch steering with the player sliding horizontally across a three-lane road while obstacles approach from above.
objective: Survive as long as possible, avoid collisions, and achieve the highest distance score in meters.
progression: An endless run that grows harder over time through rising speed and more frequent enemy spawns, ending instantly on collision before offering a quick restart.
theme: Cyberpunk arcade traffic survival with neon highways, hostile drones/vehicles, glowing city silhouettes, and sci-fi HUD styling.
mood: Fast, sleek, tense, reactive, and arcade-like with flashy success/failure feedback.
likely_audience: players who enjoy quick reflex games with futuristic presentation
confidence_notes: High confidence that the core game is an endless survival dodge game with lane-runner structure.
High confidence that score is distance-based rather than combat- or collectible-based.
Moderate confidence on whether the player avatar is best read as a car, interceptor, or hover vehicle; visuals and text blend those ideas.
High confidence that there are no upgrades, levels, story branches, or meta-progression systems in this implementation.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-friendly single-screen arcade game called "Slipstream Neon" where the player controls a glowing cyan futuristic interceptor from a top-down perspective on a three-lane neon highway at night. The game should begin on a polished start screen with cyberpunk UI, then transition into an endless survival run where the player steers horizontally by dragging or moving a finger or cursor left and right across the road. Incoming hostile traffic or rogue drone-like vehicles spawn in random lanes from the top of the screen and move downward, and the player must weave between open lanes to avoid collisions. Score should represent distance survived in meters and increase continuously during play, while the game gradually becomes harder by increasing scroll speed and reducing the delay between obstacle spawns. A collision should immediately end the run, show a stylish game-over panel with the final distance, and allow an instant restart. Present the game with a full-screen canvas, glowing lane lines, animated starfield, distant neon skyline, futuristic HUD, looping action music, short sound effects for start, pass, crash, and sound toggle, plus quick celebratory and crash feedback animations. Keep the rules simple, readable, and highly replayable, emphasizing fast reflexes, clean lane-switching, strong visual contrast, and a sleek neon sci-fi mood.
